title: Divergence Record
description: §3.1, fourth residual: 'every evaluation emits a signed divergence record — score commitment, stack measurement, threshold, and outcome — appended to the mandate's lineage, so that dispute systems consume drift evidence from the same signed chain that carries the authorization itself, rather than from a runtime's private log.' §4.4: 'The patch together with its divergence record forms the dispute-evidence bundle answering the question no current framework can: the user approved this specific deviation, after the specified presentation and authenticated confirmation, for this transaction only.' SCOPE NOTE: this schema describes the record. The scorer that produces the score is NOT part of this repository; §3.1's E₀ and E₁ are computed elsewhere and enter here only as commitments and ciphertext.

record_id.description: Identifier of this record within the mandate's lineage.

mandate_family_id.description: §5.3. The family whose lineage this record is appended to.

base_mandate_hash.description: §4.2. The mandate version against which the evaluation ran; the same value a MandatePatch carries.

checkout_commitment.description: §3.1, fifth residual: 'the input to scoring is welded to the transaction. The evaluator ... MUST compute E₁ over the canonical authorization transaction commitment defined in Section 4.3 — the same serialization whose hash binds the checkout — never over agent-relayed prose.'

deployment_variant.description: §3.1: 'wallet-side scoring (private, self-attested), gateway-side scoring (network-visible, requires cart disclosure), and TEE-attested scoring (private and third-party verifiable, with the enclave measurement covering the full pinned stack).' §7: 'the semantic predicate enters as a committed score under an attested scoring environment ... not a proof of the embedding computation itself.'

enclave_attestation.description: Attestation evidence for the TEE-attested variant; explicit null otherwise. PROFILE-DEFINED: attestation format.

scoring_stack.description: §3.1, 'stack measurement' is one of the four things every divergence record carries. §8: 'scoring-stack substitution [is answered] by whole-stack measurement with anti-rollback on stack versions.' A verifier MUST reject a record whose `stack_measurement` differs from the mandate's pinned measurement, or whose `stack_version` is lower than the mandate's.

stack_measurement.description: §3.1. Measurement of the full pinned stack as actually used.

stack_version.description: §3.1, 'a monotonic stack version that verifiers enforce against rollback'.

threshold_applied_micro.description: §3.1, 'threshold' is one of the four carried values. 'the applicable threshold is always the most conservative among matching categories'.

category_id_applied.description: §3.1. Which taxonomy category supplied `threshold_applied_micro`, under the mandate's pinned taxonomy.

aggregation.description: §3.1: 'Scoring is performed per line item with worst-case aggregation alongside any cart-level score.'

cart_level_score_commitment.description: §3.1, 'alongside any cart-level score'. Committed, not disclosed — 'authorization never rests on a single cart-centroid embedding'.

line_item_scores.description: §3.1: 'Scoring is performed per line item.' One entry per line item of the bound canonical commitment. PROFILE-DEFINED: array ordering — profile v1 requires the same ordering the canonical commitment's `line_items` are in after profile sorting.

line_id.description: Line-item identifier within the bound canonical commitment (§4.3).

score_commitment.description: §3.1. Commitment to d(E₀, E₁) for this line. The score itself is not disclosed here.

exceeded_threshold.description: §3.1. Whether this line drove the worst-case aggregate past τ.

score_commitment.description: §3.1, 'score commitment' — the first of the four values every divergence record carries. Commitment to the worst-case aggregate score.

encrypted_score.description: §3.1: 'the numeric score is encrypted to the user and issuer within the divergence record; upstream parties receive coarse reason codes.' §8: 'the mitigations are binary agent-visible outcomes, scores encrypted to principal and issuer, coarse upstream reason codes, and per-mandate attempt budgets, and the residual — slow probing across many mandates — is acknowledged.'

recipients.description: §3.1, 'encrypted to the user and issuer'. No other recipient is permitted by the paper's text.

encryption_alg.description: PROFILE-DEFINED: the paper fixes the recipients, not the algorithm.

outcome.description: §3.1, 'outcome' — the fourth carried value. 'The agent-visible outcome is strictly binary — pass or suspend.' §3.1: 'failure suspends rather than declines. When any patchable predicate fails — including the defining case in which every machine-enforceable constraint passes but d(E₀, E₁) > τ ... the authorization request enters a suspended state and the flow transitions to the Section 6 challenge, whose successful completion yields a Section 4 MandatePatch.'

reason_codes.description: §3.1: 'upstream parties receive coarse reason codes.' Deliberately coarse — a reason code MUST NOT carry the score, the threshold, or any value from which the decision boundary can be reconstructed (§3.1, §8). Empty array for a pass. PROFILE-DEFINED: the reason-code vocabulary.

flagged_line_ids.description: §4.2. Line items whose approval a MandatePatch's `value_new` may name: 'the tuple's value_new encodes the set of approved line-item identifiers within the canonical commitment — approval of those exact flagged lines, with whole-cart approval as the degenerate all-lines case.' Empty array for a pass.

failing_predicate_ids.description: §4.2: 'To prevent serial suspension fatigue, the evaluating wallet, gateway, or attested scorer MUST surface every failing predicate in the initial suspension, so that a single challenge and a single signature can cover the full tuple set.' Every failing predicate, not only the semantic one. Empty array for a pass.

cumulative_divergence_after_micro.description: §3.2: 'A cumulative divergence budget per mandate across transactions guards against semantic salami slicing, in which many individually-passing transactions drift in aggregate.' Budget consumption after this evaluation.

attempt_index.description: §3.1, 'per-mandate attempt budgets and cart-revision throttling bound iterative probing of the decision boundary.'

previous_record_hash.description: §3.1: records are 'appended to the mandate's lineage, so that dispute systems consume drift evidence from the same signed chain that carries the authorization itself, rather than from a runtime's private log.' Explicit null for the first record in a lineage.

signature.description: §3.1, 'every evaluation emits a signed divergence record'. Signed by the evaluator — wallet, gateway, or attested scorer (§4.2) — not by the principal.

kid.description: Key identifier of the signing key. PROFILE-DEFINED: the derivation. Profile v1 uses `base64url(SHA-256(SPKI DER))` without padding — the unpadded base64url encoding of the SHA-256 digest of the DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the signing public key. The identifier is therefore CONTENT-DERIVED and unambiguous without consulting any directory; a key directory only RESOLVES a `kid` to its material and validity interval, it never defines it. REQUIRED, and deliberately not optional: evidence signed without a key identifier is verifiable only by trial-verification against every historical key, which goes ambiguous the instant two keys coexist. This field is NOT retrofittable — artifacts already signed without it can never be cleanly verified after a rotation, which is why it is present from the first commit. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, which is equally content-derived but fixes the key representation to JWK rather than SPKI.

alg.description: Signature algorithm identifier, JOSE/COSE name. PROFILE-DEFINED: the disclosure constrains no algorithm suite. Profile v1 admits exactly this set — ES256/ES384/ES512, the ECDSA suite AP2 v0.2 requires of its bindings; EdDSA (Ed25519); and RS256/PS256, which appear on deployed WebAuthn authenticators. A binding profile MAY narrow this enum but MUST NOT widen it without taking a new profile identifier. This member REPLACES the former free-string `algorithm`: a free string and a constrained identifier naming the same fact can disagree, and disagreement about the algorithm is disagreement about what the signature covers.

signed_at.description: The signing instant, RFC 3339 with 'Z' and second precision — the same timestamp form every other timestamp in this repository uses (PROFILE-DEFINED, decided; profile v1 takes no epoch-integer form, so that a validity interval and an artifact's `issued_at`/`expiry` are always directly comparable). This is the instant that key-validity intervals are evaluated AGAINST: a signature verifies iff `signed_at` falls inside the [not_before, not_after] interval recorded for `kid`, and a verifier MUST verify against THE KEY CURRENT AT SIGNING TIME, NEVER THE KEY CURRENT NOW. Rejecting evidence because its signing key was rotated afterwards is a bug, not a security property — planned retirement is prospective only, and evidence anchored before it stays valid permanently. A self-asserted `signed_at` is adequate for routine verification and NOT adequate for dispute-grade evidence; see `anchor`.

signer_role.description: §4.2, 'the evaluating wallet, gateway, or attested scorer'.

domain_separation.description: §6.2 domain-separation vocabulary, applied to the record's transcript so that a record cannot be transplanted into another accepting context.

ds_tag.description: §6.2 domain-separation tag: the digest of the domain separator this signature is bound to, base64url unpadded. DISPOSITION (PROFILE-DEFINED, DECIDED — this is the choice the schema makes rather than leaves implicit): profile v1 carries `ds_tag` HERE, in the JSON body, beside the `domain_separation` components it is derived from, AND requires it to byte-equal the domain separator bound into the carrier's signed input — the WebAuthn `clientDataJSON.challenge`, or the KB-JWT `aud`/`nonce` under an SD-JWT binding. A verifier MUST recompute the tag from `domain_separation` and MUST compare it against the value bound in the carrier; a body `ds_tag` not reproduced in the carrier is NOT covered by the signature and MUST be rejected. The body copy exists so that evidence can be checked offline without a carrier parser; the carrier copy is what makes the separator signature-covered. Leaving this disposition implicit is exactly what §6.2's transplant attack needs in order to succeed, because two verifiers would otherwise disagree about whether the separator is signature-covered at all. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: carry the tag ENTIRELY in the WebAuthn/KB-JWT layer and leave only the components in the body — rejected for v1 because it makes offline evidence verification depend on a carrier parser, and because body components carrying no tag invite a verifier to treat them as authoritative when nothing signs them. PROFILE-DEFINED derivation, profile v1: SHA-256 over the ASCII prefix 'MandateLifecycle/v1/transcript' followed by LP(purpose), LP(audience), LP(relying_party), LP(mandate_family_id), LP(decimal encoding of mandate_version), LP(rail), LP(binding_profile), where LP(x) is the uint16 big-endian byte length of the UTF-8 encoding of x followed by those bytes — length-prefixed with NO delimiters, because `relying_party` and `mandate_family_id` are attacker-influenced. The prefix MUST differ from the §7 nullifier prefix ('MandateLifecycle/v1/nullifier') so that a transcript tag and a nullifier tag can never collide.

anchor.description: OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED — see the `$defs/anchor` description. Omit it and `signed_at` is self-asserted, which does not carry dispute-grade weight, because the signer is precisely the party with an incentive to misstate the signing time.

Independent evidence that a signature existed at its `signed_at`. OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED: routine verification can rely on a self-asserted `signed_at`, but dispute-grade evidence cannot, because a self-asserted timestamp is asserted by the one party with an incentive to misstate it. PROFILE-DEFINED: profile v1 anchors into the §5.2 transparency log rather than standing up a second log — §5.2 already requires 'cosigned heads or a witness network against split-view equivocation', which is precisely the property a time anchor needs, so reusing it adds a guarantee without adding an operator. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 3161 timestamp authority, which a §5.2 issuer-registry deployment needs instead, since such a deployment may run no log at all. Stapled at signing time, so dispute-time verification never depends on a service endpoint still being reachable years later.

log_id.description: Identifier of the §5.2 transparency log this signature is anchored in.

epoch.description: Log epoch whose cosigned head covers this entry — the same epoch space a supersession record advances (§5.2, §7).

inclusion_proof.description: Merkle audit path from this signature's leaf to the epoch head, ordered leaf-ward to root-ward, each sibling hash base64url unpadded. PROFILE-DEFINED: leaf encoding and the log's hash function.

hash.description: PROFILE-DEFINED hash encoding. Profile v1: SHA-256 over the JCS (RFC 8785) serialization, base64url without padding, prefixed with the algorithm name.
